source: NCERT Class VI, Curiosity: Textbook of Science, Ch. 1.

sections.heading: 1. What is Science
points: **Science** = a systematic way of studying the natural world through **observation, questioning and experiment**.
It grows from **curiosity** — asking *what, why and how* about things around us.
Science gives **knowledge**; **technology** applies that knowledge to solve problems and make tools.

sections.heading: 2. The Way of Science (Scientific Method)
points: Science values **evidence**, careful measurement and repeating tests.

sections.heading: 3. Branches of Science
points: **Physics** — matter, energy, motion, force, light, sound.
**Chemistry** — substances, their properties and changes.
**Biology** — living things (plants, animals, humans).
Also **astronomy** (space) and **earth science**.
Indian scientists: e.g. **C. V. Raman** (Raman Effect), **Jagadish Chandra Bose**, **Homi Bhabha**, **Kalpana Chawla**.

sections.heading: 4. Science All Around Us
points: Science explains everyday things — why the sky is blue, how plants grow, why ice melts.
It improves **health, food, transport and communication**.
**Asking questions** and observing carefully is the start of every scientific discovery.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Science = systematic study of nature via observation & experiment; driven by curiosity.
Scientific method: observe → question → hypothesis → experiment → analyse → conclude.
Branches: physics (matter/energy), chemistry (substances), biology (life).
Science = knowledge; technology = its application.
C. V. Raman = Raman Effect (Nobel Prize in Physics).

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Science** = knowledge of nature; **technology** = applying it — they are related but not the same.
A **hypothesis** is a testable guess, not a proven fact until experiments support it.
Physics/chemistry/biology study different aspects of the same natural world.
